key_insight: Stacking ensembles outperformed multitask neural networks in predicting UTS, weld hardness, and HAZ hardness, with the largest advantage in UTS.
engineering_relevance: Predicting weld strength and hardness can support welding-process optimization and assessment of joint performance.
method: Compare multitask neural networks and stacking ensembles on a shared welding dataset.
Use shared hidden layers and task-specific outputs in the multitask model.
Evaluate all three targets using RMSE and R².
evidence_signal: Stacking achieved R² values of 0.9863, 0.9782, and 0.8453 for UTS, weld hardness, and HAZ hardness, respectively, versus 0.6724, 0.9215, and 0.8407 for the multitask model.
watch_item: The abstract does not specify dataset size, validation design, or RMSE scaling, limiting assessment of deployment readiness.
paper_title: A Comparative Analysis of Multitask Neural Networks and Stacking Ensemble Learning for Predicting UTS, Weld Hardness, and HAZ Hardness in Welding Applications
